name: coding-voice
description: Reads the agent's answer out loud when a prompt finishes. Play/pause in the status bar, your own TTS API key, multiple languages.

commands.title: Coding Voice: Enable / disable reading aloud
Coding Voice: Set TTS API key

codingVoice.enabled.description: Read the agent's answer out loud when a turn finishes.

enumDescriptions: Built-in system voice — free, offline, no API key.
ElevenLabs — natural voices, requires your own API key.
codingVoice.engine.description: Speech engine. Cloud engines bill your own account directly.

enumDescriptions: Read only what matters — headings, highlighted sentences, the first sentence of each paragraph and the closing thought.
Read only the closing part of the answer — the conclusion and what to do next.
codingVoice.scope.description: How much of the answer to read.

codingVoice.elevenLabsVoiceId.description: Optional ElevenLabs voice ID. Leave empty to use a built-in female/male voice. Paste an ID from your ElevenLabs Voice Library to override both.

codingVoice.elevenLabsStability.description: ElevenLabs voice stability. Lower is more expressive and variable, higher is calmer and more consistent.

codingVoice.elevenLabsSimilarity.description: ElevenLabs similarity boost — how closely the output sticks to the original voice.

codingVoice.elevenLabsStyle.description: ElevenLabs style exaggeration. Higher is more stylised but slower; 0 is neutral.

codingVoice.elevenLabsSpeakerBoost.description: ElevenLabs speaker boost — strengthens resemblance to the chosen voice.

codingVoice.language.description: Spoken language. 'auto' detects it from the answer.

codingVoice.volume.description: Reading volume in percent, relative to everything else playing. Affects only this extension's voice — your system volume stays untouched.

codingVoice.maxCharacters.description: Cut the spoken text after N characters (at a sentence boundary). 0 = read the whole answer. Keeping this low reduces what cloud engines charge you.

codingVoice.skipCodeBlocks.description: Drop fenced code blocks and tables — read aloud they are noise.

codingVoice.announceProject.description: Start every summary with the project name. Helpful when several Cursor windows read aloud at once — you hear which project a summary belongs to.

codingVoice.duckSystemAudio.description: Quiet other apps while a summary is read, then restore them to their previous level. Windows: every other app (including a browser playing YouTube) is lowered per app. macOS: Music, TV, Spotify and Swinsian are lowered automatically — macOS has no public API to control a browser's volume, so a YouTube tab in Chrome/Safari is not affected there and keeps playing at its level.

codingVoice.duckLevel.description: How much of each app's own volume to keep while reading, in percent of what it was playing. 100 = untouched, 50 = half as loud, 0 = silent. Lower = quieter background. Only used when 'Duck system audio' is on.

codingVoice.duckFade.description: How long the volume fades down when reading starts and back up when it ends, in milliseconds. 0 makes it instant. Only used when 'Duck system audio' is on.

codingVoice.ring.description: Play a short ring when the agent finishes its turn and is waiting on you but has nothing to read aloud — e.g. it asked a question, proposed a plan, or only made edits. Helps you notice decision points that would otherwise be silent.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run typecheck && npm run build
